# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-32 (Extended v211)

## Setting and Time

## English Subplot Summary

**Confirmed rumors**: Fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (confirmed by Wenelle Lindmere to Rovus Prydenridge, winter Year 8).

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford for Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead for Salcombe; Fenelle followed. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for Elmhaven (winter Year 6); Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek quit milling, took brewery work (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle found Elmhaven work (summer Year 7); Marald followed within month. Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew, became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for Dungate (autumn Year 7); Vesmira Thornmere went to Dungate (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married Luena Stenenridge's only son at Ostcombe; couple lived there. Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest. Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; lived there. Matho Stenson moved from Elmhaven to Staveford (winter Year 7); Fenelle followed Marald to Ravenmere within month. Elra Corrford rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Gulhaven. Red Ismira went along to live in Staveford. Islan Thornmere died of old age at Dungate. Gadrek Prydenridge married Lura Haskick's eldest daughter in chapel at Ostcombe; couple lived there. Luvie Prydenridge and Semor wed at Ostcombe. Luena Stenenridge sent copper chalice by carrier to Yera Stenworth, who received it safely. Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair roof of chapel at Kelmere, shook on it. Havie Prydenridge never kept promise to Gadrek (pay old debt); matter abandoned. Luena Stenenridge left Wilwick, settled in Ostcombe. Rozek Stenenridge went along to live in Ostcombe. Luvie Prydenridge gave up weaving, took work as chandler (autumn Year 8). Ismira Stenson gave up being shepherd, took work as scribe (winter Year 8). Gadrek Prydenridge won copper chalice from Yera Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it (winter Year 8).

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7).

**Property transfers**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it. Kassa Brackick gave amber map to Volan Stenworth (summer Year 8). Kassa Brackick gave bone compass to Ismira (autumn Year 8).

## Marius and Cosette: Courtship, Revelation, Marriage, and Jean Valjean's Crisis

**Spring Year 6 confessions**: Marius revealed—orphan, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette revealed—raised at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent.

**Barricade and rescue (24 June)**: Éponine revealed leading Marius to barricade, gave letter from Cosette before dying. Marius joined barricade (6 June), witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed. Shot broke collar bone. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished.

**Medical recovery (Chapters 27-30)**: Bullet deflected by pocket-book, serious laceration but not dangerous. Underground journey dislocated collar-bone seriously. Arms slashed with sabre cuts. Head covered with cuts. **7 September (four months after retrieval)**: Doctor declared Marius would recover. When Marius called grandfather "father" three times, Gillenormand agreed to bring Cosette to him.

**Cosette's arrival and revelation (Chapter 31)**: Learned she was not daughter of old man she called father; he was merely kinsman; another Fauchelevent was her real father. She was so full of joy cloud did not last long. She had Marius.

**Cosette's dowry (Chapter 31)**: Five hundred eighty thousand francs constituted legacy by dead person desiring to remain unknown.

**Gillenormand's gifts**: Called Cosette "exquisite darling," "masterpiece," warned half his possessions swallowed in annuity. Overwhelmed her with gallant compliments and presents: robes, lace, parures, ivory bon-bon boxes. Furnished chamber with elegant trifles.

**Wedding ceremony (1 February 1833, church of Saint-Paul)**: **Cosette wore white taffeta petticoat, Binche guipure robe, English point veil, fine pearl necklace, orange flower wreath.** Route: Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. **Two maskers noticed wedding—Spaniard with enormous nose and huge black moustache; young girl masked with loup dressed as gaunt fishwife—held dialogue in low voice.** First coach held Cosette, Aunt Gillenormand, M. Gillenormand, Jean Valjean. Marius came in second coach. Both exchanged vows, signed registers, exchanged rings, knelt side by side under pall of white moire. **During dinner, Basque reported M. Fauchelevent suffering; injured hand paining him; begged excused; would come tomorrow. Had just taken departure.** **Jean Valjean had risen, gained antechamber unperceived during Cosette's command, left during celebration.**

**Jean Valjean's moral crisis (Chapter 31)**: In Cosette's empty bedroom: no sheets on bed. Pillow covered with ticking, without case or lace, laid on blankets. All little feminine objects Cosette attached to carried away; only heavy furniture and four walls remained. Toussaint's bed despoiled. One bed only made up—Jean Valjean's bed. **He opened inseparable portmanteau which never left him.** **Questioned: Should he force himself on this happiness? Should he treat it as belonging to him? Should he remain sort of father, half seen but respected? Should he present himself there as though he had right? Should he bring past to future?** **Remained twelve long hours of winter night, ice-cold, without raising head or uttering word. Motionless as corpse. All at once shuddered convulsively, mouth glued to Cosette's garments, kissed them; then it could be seen he was alive.**

## Javert's Death (Chapter 30)

**Moral transformation**: Javert's certainty crumbled. Duty divided within conscience. Valjean disconcerted him. All axioms crumbled. M. Madeleine reappeared behind Jean Valjean. Benevolent malefactor, merciful, gentle, helpful, clement. Javert constrained to admit monster existed. Supreme anguish was loss of certainty. Code no longer anything but stump. **Suicide (evening, Place du Châtelet)**: Took off hat, placed it on edge of quay. Tall black figure appeared erect on parapet, bent over towards Seine, drew self up, fell straight down into shadows; dull splash followed. Javert drowned.

## Marius Learns Truth (Chapter 32, morning after wedding—17 February)

**Jean Valjean's appearance and revelation**: Jean Valjean appeared very pale, eyes hollow and sunken by sleeplessness. Black coat bore weary folds. **Proclaimed: "I am an ex-convict."** Proceeding from mouth of M. Fauchelevent and entering ear of Marius overshot possible. Marius stood with mouth wide open.

**Jean Valjean's justification**: "I am an honest man. I should not be so if, through my fault, you had continued to esteem me; now that you despise me, I am so. I have that fatality hanging over me that, not being able to ever have anything but stolen consideration, that consideration humiliates me. In order that I may respect myself, it is necessary that I should be despised. Then I straighten up again. I am a galley-slave who obeys his conscience." Declared conscience implacable; duty places one in hell where one feels God beside you. Stated he had entered into engagements with himself; keeps them. Imagined scenario: if he remained silent, one day police would arrive, tear off mask, reveal his name.

**Marius's shock and initial anger**: Inward shudder of hideous enlightenment flashed through Marius; idea made him quiver. Caught glimpse of wretched destiny for himself in future. Addressed Jean Valjean almost like person angry with him for avowal. "But why do you tell me all this? Who forces you? You could have kept secret. What is your motive?"

**Cosette's intervention (Chapter 32)**: Door opened gently, Cosette's head appeared. Sweet face, hair in charming disorder, eyelids still swollen with sleep. Cried to them with smile, "so that they seemed to behold a smile at the heart of a rose." Entered in voluminous white dressing-gown with thousand folds and large sleeves falling to feet. Said she could tell news but they should know nothing of household matters; demanded to stay with husband and father. Then left again, promising to wait.

**Marius's continued anguish**: After Cosette's departure, Marius pleaded with Jean Valjean to give most sacred word of honor not to tell Cosette: "She does not know what it is, it would terrify her. What, a convict! we should be obliged to explain matters to her, to say to her: 'He is a man who has been in the galleys.' She saw the chain-gang pass by one day. Oh! My God!" Jean Valjean dropped into armchair, hid face in hands, seized with convulsion, threw himself against back of chair as though to gain breath, letting arms fall. Marius saw face inundated with tears, heard him murmur "so low that his voice seemed to issue from fathomless depths."

**State at chapter end**: Marius gradually familiarizing himself with something as unexpected as it was dreadful, beholding convict superposed before his very eyes upon M. Fauchelevent, overcome little by little by lugubrious reality, led by natural inclination of situation to recognize space which had just been placed between that man and himself.
